title: Find Customers with Orders Using EXISTS
description_markdown: Find customers in `customers` who have placed at least one completed order (`orders.order_status = 'completed'`) using an `EXISTS` subquery. Return `customer_id`, `first_name`, and `email`. Order by `customer_id`.
starter_query:
-- Use EXISTS subquery
SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email
FROM customers c
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE ...)
solution_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_status = 'completed') ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;
solution_explanation: EXISTS tests for the existence of rows in a subquery and short-circuits as soon as a match is found.
hints: Correlate the subquery on `o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_status = 'completed'`.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_status = 'completed') ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;

title: Detect Products Sold in Bulk via EXISTS
description_markdown: Use a correlated `EXISTS` subquery to find products that have been purchased with a quantity of 2 or more in at least one order line (`EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id AND oi.quantity >= 2)`). Return `p.product_id`, `p.product_name`, and `p.price`. Order by `p.product_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- EXISTS for bulk orders
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price
FROM products p
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id AND oi.quantity >= 2
)
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price FROM products p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id AND oi.quantity >= 2) ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;
solution_explanation: EXISTS short-circuits as soon as a single matching order item meeting the quantity threshold is encountered.
common_mistakes: Selecting column data inside EXISTS rather than a constant like 1.
interview_tip: SELECT 1 inside EXISTS is standard practice because the database engine ignores projection expressions during existence checks.
hints: Use `WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id AND oi.quantity >= 2)`.
Order by `p.product_id ASC`.
Query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price FROM products p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id AND oi.quantity >= 2) ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;

title: Find Products Ordered by Multiple Distinct Customers
description_markdown: Use an `IN` subquery joining `order_items` and `orders` to find products that have been purchased by at least 2 distinct customers: `product_id IN (SELECT oi.product_id FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY oi.product_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) >= 2)`. starter_query:
-- IN subquery with COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)
SELECT product_id, product_name, price
FROM products
WHERE product_id IN (
  SELECT oi.product_id FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY oi.product_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) >= 2
)
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT product_id, product_name, price FROM products WHERE product_id IN (SELECT oi.product_id FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY oi.product_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) >= 2) ORDER BY product_id ASC;

title: Verify Courses with High Passing Standards via NOT EXISTS
description_markdown: Use `NOT EXISTS` and `EXISTS` to find courses that have final exam marks recorded (`EXISTS ...`), and where NO final exam score fell below 80.00 (`NOT EXISTS ... score < 80.00`). Return `c.course_code`, `c.course_name`, and `c.department`. Order by `c.course_code` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Universal quantification with NOT EXISTS and EXISTS
SELECT c.course_code, c.course_name, c.department
FROM courses c
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id
  WHERE e.course_id = c.course_id AND m.assessment_type = 'final'
) AND NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id
  WHERE e.course_id = c.course_id AND m.assessment_type = 'final' AND m.score < 80.00
)
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT c.course_code, c.course_name, c.department FROM courses c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id WHERE e.course_id = c.course_id AND m.assessment_type = 'final') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id WHERE e.course_id = c.course_id AND m.assessment_type = 'final' AND m.score < 80.00) ORDER BY c.course_code ASC;
solution_explanation: Expresses 'for all students, score >= 80' using double negation: 'exists at least one exam AND does not exist any exam with score < 80'.
common_mistakes: Omitting the EXISTS check, which would include courses with 0 exams (vacuous truth).
interview_tip: In SQL, universal quantification ('for all') is implemented using NOT EXISTS ('there is no counterexample') plus EXISTS ('the set is not empty').
hints: Combine `EXISTS` (must have at least 1 final exam) with `NOT EXISTS` (no final exam score < 80).
Order by `c.course_code ASC`.

Query: SELECT c.course_code, c.course_name, c.department FROM courses c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id WHERE e.course_id = c.course_id AND m.assessment_type = 'final') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id WHERE e.course_id = c.course_id AND m.assessment_type = 'final' AND m.score < 80.00) ORDER BY c.course_code ASC;
